summary.name: SysAdvent (eBPF article)
summary.one_liner: A SysAdvent advent-calendar article by Ania Kapuścińska that introduces eBPF programming on Linux using the BCC Python framework, with hello-world and map examples.
use_cases: Writing a first BCC Python tracing script
Hooking custom code to kernel system calls
Measuring Go binary function duration with uprobes
Choosing between kprobes and static tracepoints
summary.what_it_does: The page is an article explaining eBPF, a restricted C dialect whose programs are checked by a verifier and attached to kernel or user-space events. It walks through a hello-world program that hooks the clone syscall using BCC, with the Python side reading output from a perf ring buffer. It also covers the simpler bpf_trace_printk approach, the hook point types (kprobes, kretprobes, uprobes, uretprobes, tracepoints, XDP), and BPF maps, including a hash-table example that times a Go binary. It ends with pointers to the BCC repo, ebpf.io and an eBPF awesome list.
notable: Step-by-step progression from a perf-buffer hello world to a one-line BCC version
Explains kprobes, uprobes, tracepoints and XDP hook points
Shows BPF maps used for communication between BPF programs
caveats: Requires a Linux machine with a fairly recent kernel that supports eBPF
Examples need root privileges and the Python bcc package installed
Printing via trace_pipe is described as not recommended for real-world tools
